slides.title: The US opportunity
K-beauty is where US facial skincare is growing: its sales nearly doubled in four years while the category grew 22%

evidence: 22% All facial skincare growth, 2021–25

claims.claim: K-beauty took a share of new sales far above its share of the market
evidence: 39% K-beauty share of the category's growth, 2021–25

claims.claim: K-beauty brands: grew in every year, a steady trend rather than one viral season
For Onsoo: entering in 2027 means riding a segment that is still taking share
A 2026 trade-press figure of $5.2B for the US K-beauty market also counts makeup and hair care, so it is not comparable and not used

slides.title: Onsoo already has US demand, with monthly Amazon pilot sales nearly doubling between January and June 2026

1.9x June units as a multiple of January units

slides.title: Why not a retail-led launch
At Onsoo's current awareness, a retail launch would sell about 2.6 units per door a week and lose the shelf

claims.claim: Option B assumes Onsoo performs like a brand five times better known
evidence: Median units per door per week, year one, by aided awareness, 2025: Below 10% 2.6; 10–20% 3.5; Above 20% 4.6; Option B plan 4.5
Removal threshold 4.0

claims.claim: Below 10%: Onsoo sits here
evidence: aided awareness of 4% among recent skincare buyers and 9% among K-beauty buyers

claims.claim: 10–20%: even double or triple today's awareness leaves the median newcomer below the line
Option B plan: 4.5 units a week comes from the retailer's deck on successful newcomers, the top band's result

slides.title: Even with the assumed Amazon halo, retail recovers only 31% of its $30M fixed cost, a $23M cash drain by 2030

slides.title: Only the retail-led route breaks the $18M cash cap, crossing it in 2029 and still falling in 2030

claims.claim: Only the retail-led route breaks the $18M cash cap

Amazon-led at 32%: the cap is never at risk, but payback slips past 2030

slides.title: Why Amazon-led
Advertising is the largest cost Onsoo controls in each $24 Amazon sale, and it decides the $4.73 left per unit

claims.claim: Fees are fixed by Amazon; ad efficiency is Onsoo's lever
evidence: $ per unit at 25% ad cost: Price 24; Referral fee 3.6; Fulfillment fee 5.1; Product cost 3.5; Freight and duty 1.075; Advertising 6; Contribution 4.725

claims.claim: Amazon fees: referral and fulfillment take 36% of the price and cannot be negotiated
Product: landed cost is 19% of the price, which keeps the price edge 52% of K-beauty triers value
Advertising: each percentage point of ad cost moves contribution by $0.24 a unit
evidence: Contribution per unit at the pilot's 28% ad cost: $4.01 ($10.73 before ads − $24 × 28%)
Contribution per unit at the agency median of 32%: $3.05 ($10.73 before ads − $24 × 32%)
Briefing pack, Table 4: referral fee 15% of price, FBA $5.10, ex-factory $3.50, freight $0.55, duty 15% of ex-factory cost

slides.title: What the plan must survive
Amazon-led pays back by 2030 only if ad cost averages below about 28.6% of sales, just above the pilot

claims.claim: 28.6% average ad cost at which cumulative cash is back to zero at end-2030
evidence: Cumulative cash end-2030 $M: Plan 25% 2.4; Pilot 28% 0.376; Pilot 28%, duty 25% -0.63; Agency median 32% -2.321; Agency high 38% -6.368
$6.9 per unit left for ads after fees, product and $3.87 of fixed cost per unit ÷ $24 Amazon price per unit = 28.6% break-even average ad cost of sales

claims.claim: Each percentage point of ad cost moves 2030 cumulative cash by about $0.67M
Tariff: a duty rise to 25% from 2028 lowers the break-even to about 27.1%, below the pilot
Bounded downside: even at 38%, the route stays inside the cash cap and the 8% margin floor
evidence: Agency benchmark, brands scaling from $5M to $20M a year on Amazon US: median 32%, range 26–38%

We back the CEO's Amazon-first plan, with a later retail trigger and an ad-cost gate the board can track

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Approve the Amazon-led launch in March 2027, gating ad cost now and retail on awareness: keep the CEO's Amazon-first plan, but move the retail trigger from 15% to 20% awareness, gate ad cost at the pilot's 28% after 12 months (above it, hold SKU and ad expansion and keep Japan as the 2028 fallback), enter retail only via a small door test kept at 4.0+ units a week, and put US-compliant labels on every unit from launch.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended route; meets all three limits at the pilot's ad cost; short of $40M (reaches 66% of the ambition in 2030).

Rejected: breaks the cash cap, payback and margin floor; margin below 8% in 2027–29; at current awareness would sell about 2.6 units per door a week and lose the shelf; recovers only 31% of its $30M fixed cost even with the assumed Amazon halo.

Meets the limits but builds no US business; adds only a quarter of the US route's 2030 revenue ($7M vs $26.4M); kept as the 2028 fallback if the US ad-cost gate fails; management can run only one launch in 2027.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO's initial hypothesis (Amazon in 2027, specialty retail from 2029, 15% awareness trigger, national retail launch)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Backed, with changes: retail trigger moved to above 20% awareness among category buyers, an ad-cost gate at 28% added, retail entry as a small door test instead of a national launch, US labels from launch.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Payback by 2030 needs average ad cost below about 28.6%; the agency median is 32% (range 26–38%); at 32% payback slips past 2030
The plan assumes 25% ad cost; the pilot ran at 28% on a small budget; cost per click rises as brands bid on broader keywords
A duty rise to 25% from 2028 lowers the break-even to about 27.1%, below the pilot; US duty decision expected mid-2027
Repeat purchase is 29%, below the 31% US first-year benchmark and Korea's 48%; four more SKUs may raise it but a rise is unproven
2027 needs 25,000 units a month, 1.8 times June's pace, carried by four more SKUs
The planning team applies the hero product's economics to all SKUs
Option B's 1.3 times Amazon halo is an assumption resting on a 0.71 correlation that does not show doors cause Amazon sales
Option B's 4.5 units a week assumes Onsoo performs like a brand five times better known
Japan figures use operating profit and Japan revenue (no working-capital inputs given)
No route reaches $40M by 2030; Amazon-led reaches 66%; precedent: only one of three Amazon-first entrants passed $5M
Built only from the briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck had no pictures; charts came as extracted data series. Waterfall charts on slides 9, 12 and 16 have a 'base' (invisible) series, which I left out of the evidence. Chart shares on slide 5 came as decimals and are shown as percentages. On slide 13 the A row shows peak cash at −$2.4M and end-2030 cash at $0.4M at the 28% ad cost, while slides 10 and 23 show 25% ad-cost values ($2.4M at end-2030). I copied these numbers as given and did not reconcile them. Slide 14's headline says Japan adds 'a quarter' of US revenue and slide 2 says 'nearly four times'; both are kept as stated. Slide 21's roadmap is a grid of timeline cells, so the half-year placement of each item could not be fully recovered from the plain-text extraction.
